assumptions: The source node postcondition of achieved unprivileged local code execution is a generated claim, while the CVE text only says the attacker can 'potentially execute code'.
The target node postcondition of escalation to NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM is a generated claim; the CVE text supports 'local privilege escalation' but not the exact SYSTEM outcome.
Same-host deployment between the Oculus Browser execution context and Windows Oculus Desktop/OVRServiceLauncher.exe is an inference, never a fact.
The browser execution context can capture and abuse the leaked privileged process handle is an inference, never a fact.
Version applicability and platform compatibility are unverified without environment observations.

evidence_quotes.quote: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI
allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code
an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process
This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.

response.reason: CVE-2019-3562's actual described effect is remote HTML injection into the Oculus Browser UI, enabling UI spoofing and only 'potentially execute code'; it does not establish achieved unprivileged process execution. CVE-2021-24038 requires an unprivileged process on an affected Oculus Desktop host with OVRServiceLauncher.exe and describes a handle-management bug that could expose a privileged process handle, leading to local privilege escalation. The edge overreaches by treating potential browser code execution as a confirmed local execution context and by assuming that context is on the same host and can capture and abuse the leaked handle. A bounded causal bridge is plausible only if same-host deployment, actual attacker-controlled execution, target version, and handle accessibility are verified. Therefore the edge is conditional and cannot enter a strict graph as supported without those missing conditions.
